doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Food Network theme for Bobby Flay's show
summary: Levin describes writing the theme for Bobby Flay's first show with director Wayne Page on a low-budget production.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. And you go from something like that to Food Channel TV series. So when you get contracted for something like this, does the producer have suggestions for you?

Yes. These days more suggestions than we probably like. That particular one, the Bobby Flay show, the original show, it was actually the director who came, his name is Wayne Page, a TV director that I’ve worked with, I’ve known him for years and done odds and ends projects for him. This was a case where he was doing “Hot Off the Grill” it was Bobby’s first show. And they just wanted a theme. So he came to me and sat and watched over my shoulder while I created it. And that was it. It was fun to do. It was actually a low budget production. The food channel doesn’t pay any residuals, so I didn’t get too deep into it, because there’s a lot of that on cable TV which is unfortunate.
